verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents service keys for AI agent automation and MCP servers. The keys are decoupled from user accounts and can be limited to specific scopes instead of full tenant access, which directly delivers least-privilege credentials for an agent. An OAuth alternative also confines the assistant to the connecting member's role. missing for 10: an enumerated list of available scopes, documentation of key expiry/rotation/revocation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Service keys are decoupled from user accounts and can be scoped for specific tasks.
Grant Full access to all tenant service-key scopes, or choose Limit access to… to grant only specific scopes.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows, and every action is attributed to your account.
